About Revolut

People deserve more from their money. More visibility, more control, and more freedom. Since 2015, Revolut has been on a mission to deliver just that. Our powerhouse of products — including spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more — help our 80+ million customers get more from their money every day.

As we continue our lightning-fast growth,‌ 2 things are essential to our success: our people and our culture. In recognition of our outstanding employee experience, we've been certified as a Great Place to Work™. So far, we have 13,000+ people working around the world, from our offices and remotely, to help us achieve our mission. And we're looking for more brilliant people. People who love building great products, redefining success, and turning the complexity of a chaotic world into the simplicity of a beautiful solution.

About The Role

Financial Crime Operations is at the forefront of Revolut’s efforts to keep customers and their money safe. Team members work directly with customers to resolve issues and flag potential concerns. Using cutting-edge technology and sharp attention to detail, they help prevent financial crime and keep trust at the core of Revolut.

We’re looking for an External Enquiry Analyst to detect and investigate risks that could impact our customers. You’ll work closely with the Compliance team to safeguard funds and ensure robust protection against financial crime.

Up to shape what's next in finance? Let's get in touch.

What You'll Be Doing

• Liaising with law enforcement and the Legal team as necessary
• Responding to court orders, DPAs, and POs, and complying with legislation, like POCA and DPA
• Ensuring requests are completed within the applicable time scales
• Preparing documentation for third-party requests
• Conducting fraud-related investigations based on reports received
• Generating reports and creating alerts for suspicious activity
• Discussing financial crime concerns with stakeholders across departments

What You'll Need

• A bachelor's degree (must be able to provide a certificate)
• Fluency in German (C2)
• Fluency in English (C1+)
• 2+ years of FinCrime experience, or 1+ years experience dealing with external law enforcement and other government agencies
• Familiarity with investigative methodologies evidenced by use of analytical tools (e.g., spreadsheets, filters, pivots, network charts)
• Knowledge of court orders, DPA, PO, and preparing witness statements
• Confidence communicating with people at all levels, both externally and within the organisation
• Critical thinking skills
• Impeccable attention to detail
• The ability to multitask, prioritise, and work well under pressure

Nice to have

• Fluency in other languages
• A degree in law or STEM subject
• A professional certification (ICA or ACAMS)

Building a global financial super app isn’t enough. Our Revoluters are a priority, and that’s why in 2021 we launched our inaugural D&I Framework, designed to help us thrive and grow everyday. We're not just doing this because it's the right thing to do. We’re doing it because we know that seeking out diverse talent and creating an inclusive workplace is the way to create exceptional, innovative products and services for our customers. That’s why we encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences to join this multicultural, hard-working team.

Important notice for candidates:

Job scams are on the rise. Please keep these guidelines in mind when applying for any open roles.

• Only apply through official Revolut channels. We don’t use any third-party services or platforms for our recruitment.
• Always double-check the emails you receive. Make sure all communications are being done through official Revolut emails, with an @revolut.com domain.

We won't ask for payment or personal financial information during the hiring process. If anyone does ask you for this, it’s a scam. Report it immediately.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for an experienced Mobile Fraud Analyst to join our team and take an active role in detecting, investigating, and preventing fraud across our mobile and roaming services.

This position is specifically focused on fraud within the mobile telecommunications industry, including cellular traffic, roaming, Voice, SMS, Data, SIM/eSIM, and international traffic.

Previous hands-on experience with fraud in the mobile/telecommunications industry is mandatory.

What You'll Do:

• Monitor and analyze mobile traffic to identify suspicious activity, abnormal usage patterns, and potential fraud.
• Investigate fraud cases across Voice, SMS, Data, Roaming, SIM/eSIM, and international traffic.
• Identify telecom-specific fraud patterns, including unusual calling behavior, high-volume traffic, suspicious destinations, SIM misuse, traffic pumping, and other fraudulent activities.
• Analyze CDRs and telecom usage records to identify anomalies and suspicious behavior.
• Investigate fraud incidents and identify the root cause, affected subscribers, SIMs, devices, networks, and destinations.
• Assess the financial impact and exposure of fraud incidents.
• Define, maintain, and continuously improve fraud detection rules, thresholds, alerts, and monitoring mechanisms.
• Recommend and coordinate preventive actions, including blocking or restricting suspicious subscribers, SIMs, destinations, networks, or traffic patterns.
• Work closely with Network, Roaming, Operations, Product, Finance, and other relevant teams during fraud investigations.
• Track fraud trends and proactively identify new risks, vulnerabilities, and fraud patterns.
• Prepare reports and management-level summaries regarding fraud incidents, trends, financial exposure, and preventive actions.

Requirements:

Requirements:

• 3+ years of experience in Mobile/Telecom Fraud Analysis, Fraud Prevention, or a similar telecom fraud role.
• Previous fraud-related experience within a Mobile Network Operator (MNO), MVNO, roaming provider, or telecommunications company – mandatory.
• Strong understanding of mobile telecommunications, cellular traffic, and roaming environments.
• Experience investigating Voice and SMS fraud.
• Knowledge of CAMEL, VoLTE, Diameter, OCS, and telecom charging systems.
• Experience working with CDRs and telecom usage data.
• Strong SQL and data analysis skills.
• Ability to analyze large volumes of traffic and identify abnormal patterns and anomalies.
• Strong analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to independently manage fraud investigations from detection through root-cause analysis and mitigation.
• High attention to detail, ownership, and ability to respond quickly to critical fraud incidents.
• Experience working with AI tools (ChatGPT, OpenAI API, Claude, Gemini, etc.).
• Strong English communication skills.

Nice to Have:

• Experience with international roaming fraud and wholesale telecom environments.
• Experience working with TAP files and roaming records.
• Familiarity with IMSI, ICCID, MSISDN, IMEI, MCC/MNC, VPLMN, and HPLMN.
• Experience working with Telecom Fraud Management Systems (FMS).
• Experience with Python, Power BI, or other analytical and automation tools.
• Experience developing automated fraud detection, monitoring, and alerting mechanisms.

About Webbing:

Founded in early 2010, Webbing is a global data MVNO that delivers enterprise grade, global connectivity and IoT services across more than 200 countries and 600+ mobile carriers' networks. Webbing's secured network delivers network protection and web content intelligence.

Enterprise customers can manage, monitor, and optimize data usage in real-time with Webbing's powerful software platform. Gain visibility by application type and have the power to white list applications and limit non-business applications with the click of a button, saving money and improving compliance.

What we offer:

• An exciting and challenging workplace with great skill and knowledge development opportunities.
• The opportunity to join a team of highly professional specialists in an international environment.
• The opportunity for professional development within a reputable international innovative and growing company.
• Meal Vouchers.
• Medical insurance.

Discover ING Hubs Romania

ING Hubs Romania offers 130 services in software development, data management, non-financial risk & compliance, audit, and retail operations to 24 ING units worldwide, with the help of over 2000 high-performing engineers, risk, and operations professionals.

We started out in 2015 as ING’s software development hub, then steadily expanded our range to include more services and competencies. Now we provide borderless services with bank-wide capabilities and operate from our office in Bucharest. 

Our tech capabilities remain the core of our business, with more than 1800 colleagues active in Data Management, Touchpoint Channels & Integration, Core Banking, and Global Products.

We enjoy a flexible way of working and a highly collaborative environment, where fair and constructive feedback is encouraged.

For us, impact isn't a perk. It's the driver of our work. We are guided and rewarded by a shared desire to make the world a better place, one innovative solution at a time. Our colleagues make it their job to do impactful things and they love doing it in good company. Do you?

The Mission

Within ING, there is ING Analytics (INGA) - a major driving force in its digital transformation of the bank. By creating measurable value for ING and its customers through world-class analytics products and services, INGA helps ING to become a data-driven leader. Among others, INGA delivers call & speech analytics, generative AI in risk summarization, insights into portfolio performance, advanced ESG data insights (commercial purposes), data analytics platforms (cloud and on-premises), and many more.

We are looking for a Data Scientist to join us in Bucharest. In this role, you will be responsible for scoping, developing, validating, and documenting machine-learning-based solutions which will form the core of the products that INGA develops. You will collaborate closely with other scientists and analysts in evaluating model performance to ensure the best possible performance.

We are looking for curious and empathetic individuals who are committed to developing themselves and learning new skills. We hire people based on an evaluation of their potential and support them throughout their time in Bucharest. Come join us!

Your day-to-day

A typical day for a data scientist starts with coffee, catching up with colleagues, and drafting a plan for the coming day. After the standup, you will start developing machine learning solutions, adopting best practices and quality standards for fit-for-purpose model pipelines. As an effective team member of the model development & implementation team, you will challenge the status quo while addressing the requirements of the ING model governance.

After lunch, you will prepare fraud advance models to be deployed to production. Finally, to wrap up the day, you will actively explore INGA’s domain and engage in creating a journey that makes our bank and our society safer.

What You’ll Bring To The Team

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, mathematics, engineering, or econometrics.
• 3-5 years of work experience in the data science field.
• Good understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods.
• Strong Python programming skills, Apache Spark, SQL, Git.
• Excellent communication skills, capable of working collaboratively in a semi-remote, globally distributed team.

Nice to have

• Broad experience with end-to-end machine learning projects; involvement in all modeling steps (from data extraction to production).
• Background in writing production-ready code and a solid understanding of object-oriented programming is a strong plus.
• Proactive and can-do attitude (self-steering).
• Curious mindset; you are collaborative and passionate about helping others to grow and improve.
• Able to embrace challenges in a fast-changing and complex environment.

If you want to deep dive into the processing of personal data conducted by ING Hubs Romania during the recruitment process and your rights related to it, read the privacy notices on our website (make sure to scroll until you reach the Data Protection section/ Candidates tab).

Job Description - 
• Execute control testing and maintain documentation for SOX compliance.
• Assist in walkthroughs and evidence gathering for audits.
• Track remediation activities and update control logs.
• Support process owners in control implementation.
• Contribute to compliance reporting and process improvements.
• Lead SOX control testing activities across assigned business processes and locations.
• Review control documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance with SOX requirements.
• Coordinate with control owners and stakeholders to resolve testing issues and control deficiencies.
• Evaluate control design and operating effectiveness, identifying risks and improvement opportunities.
• Assess the impact of process, system, and organizational changes on the SOX control environment.
• Monitor remediation plans and validate the timely closure of identified control deficiencies.
• Prepare and present testing results, risk assessments, and compliance status reports to management.
• Partner with Internal Audit, External Audit, Finance, and IT teams to support audit activities and compliance initiatives.
• Perform risk assessments and contribute to annual SOX scoping and planning activities.
• Ensure control evidence meets audit standards and supports regulatory requirements.
• Provide guidance and training to process owners on internal control practices and SOX requirements.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of the control framework.
• Review and update Risk and Control Matrices (RCMs), process narratives, and flowcharts.
• Identify emerging compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigating controls.
• Support the development and implementation of governance, risk, and compliance best practices.
• Mentor junior team members and provide oversight on testing methodologies and documentation quality.

Are you ready to join our digital revolution journey?

At Aleph , we’re not just part of the digital advertising landscape—we’re shaping its future. Representing the world’s leading platforms, including TikTok, Amazon, Google, and nearly 55 others, we operate in 130+ markets across new and existing geographies.

Our mission is to empower advertisers and brands to unlock the full potential of these platforms' advertising capabilities. By fostering long-lasting partnerships, we create limitless opportunities for people and businesses to advertise effectively at both local and global levels.

With a presence spanning continents, Aleph offers you the chance to be part of a fast-growing, innovative team where your work makes a direct impact. If you’re ambitious, forward-thinking, and eager to thrive in a dynamic, global environment, Aleph is the perfect place to build your career.

Role Purpose

As Audit & Compliance Manager, Europe, you will be the primary owner of audit readiness and tax regulatory compliance across all Europe entities. You will set the standard, structure and cadence for how the region prepares for and manages statutory audits, global group audits, and tax authority engagement — working through the local reporting teams and external accountants who handle data preparation, review and submission, rather than performing that work yourself. Your role is to define how things get done, ensure consistent quality across every market, and be the region's face in front of auditors and tax authorities.

What Makes This Role Different

• Build, don't just maintain. You're stepping into a newly created position with a mandate to design the region's audit and compliance approach from the ground up — not inherit a fixed process. 
• Full regional ownership. This role spans the entire Europe region. 
• High visibility, real stakes. You'll be the direct point of contact with external auditors and tax authorities on some of the company's most sensitive matters, with senior leadership relying on your judgment. 
• A technology-forward environment. The business is actively investing in automation, AI and dashboarding to modernize reporting — you'll be expected to bring ideas here, not just adopt what's handed to you. 
• Cross-functional reach. You'll work closely with the Tax, Transfer Pricing and Legal teams, and directly with hub-entity finance teams, on issues spanning VAT, customer transactions and company-wide reviews. 

What You'll Do

• Statutory & Global Audit Leadership
• Audit Lifecycle Ownership: Lead the end-to-end process for local statutory audits and global group audits across all 23 countries — planning, coordinating PBC (Provided by Client) lists, and driving on-time sign-off. 
• External Auditor Relationship: Act as the primary regional point of contact for audit firms, owning timelines and resolution of open items. 
• Consolidation Alignment: Ensure local statutory filings align with Global/Group reporting timelines (IFRS/US GAAP/local GAAP) for a seamless audit process. 
• Pre-Audit Structuring: Work with local teams ahead of each audit cycle to define what needs to be prepared and how — so the region walks into every audit with a consistent, proactive structure rather than reacting to auditor requests. 
• Tax Governance & Regulatory Compliance
• Filing Oversight: Ensure accurate, on-time submission across VAT, Withholding Tax (WHT), Corporate Income Tax, and country-specific statistical and national bank reporting — delivered through local reporting teams and external accountants, with you owning quality and timeliness. 
• Tax Team Liaison: Standardize and oversee submission of supporting data to the central Tax team; ensure schedules provided for assessments are reconciled and audit-ready. 
• Notice & Assessment Management: Proactively manage tax notices and audits, coordinating evidence-gathering and working with the Tax team to ensure timely, well-supported responses. 
• Corporate Secretarial Support: Oversee annual filings and coordinate with Legal on board meeting minutes (financial aspects) and other local regulatory requirements. 
• Process Improvement & Digital Transformation
• Root Cause Analysis: Identify recurring audit adjustments or tax queries and implement structural fixes to eliminate them at the source. 
• Internal Controls: Strengthen the control environment across the region to minimize audit findings. 
• Technology & Automation: Identify and champion tools — including AI and dashboarding — to reduce manual work and increase consistency across the region's reporting. 

What We're Looking For

Mindset & Soft Skills (critical to this role)

• A challenger, not a process-follower — someone who questions how things are done today and proposes a better way, rather than simply executing an existing playbook. 
• Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, high-volume, occasionally chaotic environment, and energized rather than fatigued by it. 
• Strong communicator and team player who can build trust quickly across Tax, Legal, Transfer Pricing and local finance teams. 
• Strategic mindset with the ability to zoom out across markets while staying close enough to the detail to be credible with auditors and tax authorities. 

Experience & Technical Skills

• Currently operating at Manager level (or equivalent) within an audit firm or a multinational's in-house compliance/audit function — this is not a developmental hire. 
• 10–12+ years of post-qualification experience, with hands-on exposure to multi-country compliance in Europe. 
• Chartered Accountant (CA), CPA, or ACCA qualification. 
• Solid working knowledge of IFRS, European tax regulations, and Transfer Pricing fundamentals. 
• Advanced proficiency with Tier-1 ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or NetSuite). 
• Fluent English, written and spoken — required given daily interaction with regional and global stakeholders. 
• Strong project management and negotiation skills, with the ability to work confidently across time zones and cultures. 

In line with the EU Pay Transparency Directive, we are committed to fair and open compensation practices. For this role, the minimum gross annual base salary is 220,800 RON.

In addition to base salary, this role includes a variable component, paid annually. The final offer will reflect your experience, skills, and the scope of the role.

Aleph is a place of many cultures, perspectives, and talents. We support each other, creating an environment of giving and receiving. We value partnership and communication because we believe it takes a group of people to achieve great things. We are energized by our ever-changing industry, our curiosity keeps us learning and seeking out new opportunities.

Company Description

Since its spin-off in September 2025 AUMOVIO continues the business of the former Continental group sector Automotive as an independent company. The technology and electronics company offers a wide-ranging portfolio that makes mobility safe, exciting, connected, and autonomous. This includes sensor solutions, displays, braking and comfort systems as well as comprehensive expertise in software, architecture platforms, and assistance systems for software-defined vehicles. In the fiscal year 2024 the business areas, which now belong to AUMOVIO, generated sales of 19.6 billion Euro. The company is headquartered in Frankfurt, Germany and has about 87.000 employees in more than 100 locations worldwide.

Job Description

The AI Compliance Officer supports the design, implementation and continuous improvement of AUMOVIO’s AI Governance and AI Compliance Management System across the value chain. The role supports ensuring that AI systems, whether provided as standalone services or embedded within our products, are developed, deployed, and used in compliance with applicable laws, internal policies, and responsible AI principles.

Main Responsibilities Are

• Support the Head of Privacy and AI Compliance with the design, implementation and operation of an AI Compliance Management System, including rule framework, procedures, standards, controls, reporting and continuous improvement measures with particular focus on the EU AI Act and automotive-specific. 
• Support with the continuous implementation and completeness of an inventory of AI systems and AI-enabled tools used across the organization, including internal tools, embedded product-related AI and third-party solutions.. 
• Coordinate AI risk classification and applicability assessments under the EU AI Act and related regulatory frameworks, including the distinction between provider, deployer, importer, distributor and product-related obligations and provide expert guidance on the regulatory obligations associated with each role and risk category. 
• Advise business on compliant AI use, including high-risk AI systems, transparency requirements, prohibited AI practices, human oversight, data governance, accuracy, robustness, and post-market monitoring. 
• Support AI impact assessments, fundamental rights impact assessments, data protection impact assessments and risk reviews for AI systems, particularly where personal data, employee data, safety-critical applications or automated decision-making are involved. 
• Closely collaborate with other functions to align AI compliance activities with automotive development, validation and lifecycle processes, including interfaces to functional safety, cybersecurity, software updates and type-approval related requirements. 
• Review AI-related supplier, customer and partner arrangements in cooperation with Legal, Procurement, Data Protection and Cybersecurity, including contractual requirements, audit rights, data usage, documentation duties and allocation of responsibilities along the AI value chain. 
• Develop and deliver AI compliance trainings and awareness measures including AI literacy requirements and practical guidance on responsible use of AI tools. 
• Monitor regulatory developments, industry standards and authority guidance relevant to AI, data protection, and automotive compliance, and translate them into internal implementation actions. 
• Support audits, assessments, management reporting and incident handling related to AI systems, including documentation of findings, remediation actions and lessons learned. 

Qualifications

• University degree in Law, Compliance, Business Administration, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security or a comparable qualification. 
• At least 5 years of professional experience in compliance, legal, data protection, IT governance, product compliance, cybersecurity, risk management or a related field; experience in an international automotive, technology or manufacturing environment is strongly preferred. 
• Sound understanding of the EU AI Act, GDPR and related governance requirements; familiarity with AI risk management, human oversight, data governance and transparency obligations is a strong asset. 
• Ability to understand technical concepts related to AI, machine learning, data analytics, software development and connected vehicle ecosystems, and to translate them into practical compliance requirements. 
• Strong project management, stakeholder management and analytical skills, with the ability to coordinate cross-functional implementation activities in a matrix organization. 
• Excellent communication and drafting skills, with the ability to explain complex regulatory and technical topics clearly to both expert and non-expert audiences. 
• Fluent English language skills, spoken and written; additional language skills are an advantage. 
• High integrity, sound judgment, intercultural competence and a pragmatic, solution-oriented working style. 

Additional Information

Ready to take your career to the next level? The future of mobility isn’t just anyone’s job. Make it yours! Join AUMOVIO. Own What’s Next.

We are seeking an experienced Export Controls & Trade Compliance Specialist to provide expert advisory support on export control compliance across Vodafone Group. This role is focused on ensuring compliance with UK, EU, and US export control regulations, including dual-use items, telecommunications technology, semiconductors, encryption, cloud and AI services, and intangible technology transfers. The successful candidate will play a key role in risk mitigation, compliance transformation, stakeholder engagement, export classification, licensing, regulatory horizon scanning, and the continuous improvement of export control processes. This position requires deep technical expertise, strong analytical capabilities, and the ability to communicate complex regulatory requirements to a broad range of stakeholders.

What You’ll Do

• Review, analyse and approve exports of tangible and intangible goods, software and technology, ensuring compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements 
• Manage Group export licence applications, oversee compliance with licence conditions and support relationships with regulatory authorities 
• Contribute to Vodafone’s Trade Compliance transformation programme, supporting process optimisation, licence management enhancements and classification governance 
• Monitor emerging regulatory developments and assess potential impacts on Vodafone, including semiconductor restrictions, cloud and AI controls, China-related measures and updates to EU Regulation 2021/821

• Drive improvements to export control processes through automation, standardisation, digital workflows and centralised licence management 
• Support incident management and escalation activities where potential export control or sanctions-related risks are identified

• EU Regulation 2021/821 (Dual-Use Regulation)
• UK Export Control Order 2008
• US Export Administration Regulations (EAR), including de minimis requirements, Foreign Direct Product Rules and Entity List implications
• Strong experience in product and technology export classification covering encryption, software, cloud services, AI-enabled technologies and telecommunications network equipment

• Knowledge of freight forwarder oversight and compliance requirements 
• Understanding of sanctions-driven export restrictions affecting technology, semiconductor and military end-use or end-user activities 
• Experience designing and implementing digital-first controls, workflow automation and centralised compliance frameworks 
• Strong analytical capability with experience identifying, assessing and mitigating export control compliance risks 
• Proven experience working within complex product portfolios and multiple jurisdictions, particularly in environments subject to US EAR and EU Regulation 2021/821

• Experience working across multiple international markets with strong cross-cultural awareness 
• Fluency in English is essential. Additional language capabilities would be beneficial 
• Relevant degree qualification

The Compliance function is responsible for promoting a strong compliance culture and supporting the safe, sustainable growth of OKX. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on regulatory obligations, conduct expectations and enterprise risks.

OKX Europe Markets Limited operates within a significant EU regulatory perimeter as a MiFID II investment firm authorised under the Investment Services Act (Cap. 370), providing dealing on own account and execution of orders on behalf of clients on a matched-principal basis, together with trustee, custodian and nominee services, across the EEA on a cross-border services passport. Our product range includes crypto-asset perpetuals and expiry futures, single stock and ETF-linked futures, commodity futures and crypto-asset options, and is expanding into money market fund and structured product offerings.

About the Opportunity

As the Senior Compliance Analyst for OKX Europe Markets Limited, you will deliver the day-to-day operational compliance work of a fast-growing MiFID II investment firm: financial promotions review, complaints administration, regulatory and trade reporting support, monitoring testing and the firm's regulatory registers.

This is a high-volume, execution-focused role. The function reviews in the order of seventeen pieces of marketing and promotional material each week and handles around five new complaints each week, both scaling with a client base that is growing towards 100,000 users, alongside recurring regulatory reporting, token-listing and licence-extension assessments and compliance monitoring testing. You will be the person who keeps that machinery running accurately and on time.

You will gain broad exposure to MFSA supervision and EU financial services regulation, and direct visibility of how a MiFID II derivatives business is controlled in practice.

The position reports to the Deputy Head of Compliance, with a secondary reporting line to the Head of Compliance and MLRO, OKX Europe Markets Limited.

You will:

• 
Review client-facing marketing material and financial promotions for compliance with MiFID II fair, clear and not misleading standards and the MFSA advertisement rules, across paid and organic social, email, landing pages, banners, push notifications, video and KOL briefs, and prepare them for approval by the Deputy Head of Compliance or the Head of Compliance.

•

Support trade and transaction reporting obligations, including data collection and validation, regulatory return preparation, review and sign-off coordination, submission and evidence retention.

• 
Conduct scheduled and ad-hoc testing under the Compliance Monitoring Programme, document findings, track remediation actions to closure and maintain the monitoring calendar.

• 
Prepare token-listing and licence-extension assessments and supporting documentation for review, and support new product and feature compliance reviews and local launch sign-off.

• 
Maintain the firm's core regulatory registers — regulatory correspondence, breaches, advertisements and the regulatory obligation register — ensuring an accurate, audit-ready flow of information to the MFSA and internal stakeholders.

Draft and update compliance policies, procedures and entity-specific addenda for review and approval, in line with regulatory developments.

• 
Support regulatory-change horizon scanning, recording applicable changes against the obligation register and flagging implementation requirements.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AML Investigator based in Romania.

As an AML Investigator, you will play a key role in protecting the integrity and security of a global digital asset trading environment. You will investigate unusual and potentially suspicious activities, assess financial crime risks, and determine whether cases require regulatory reporting or can be closed with documented justification. Working within an international Compliance team, you will collaborate with fellow investigators, legal professionals, and customer support specialists to address money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud, and sanctions-related risks. You will use blockchain analytics tools and investigative techniques to identify suspicious transaction patterns and understand complex financial activities. This role combines independent decision-making, analytical thinking, and regulatory expertise in a fast-paced cryptocurrency environment. You will also have opportunities to deepen your knowledge of blockchain technology and contribute to strengthening global financial crime prevention practices.

Accountabilities

• Conduct thorough investigations into unusual and potentially suspicious activities referred to the Compliance team, ensuring timely and effective case resolution within applicable regulatory deadlines. 
• Assess financial crime risks, including money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud, and sanctions violations, within digital asset transactions and customer activities. 
• Determine whether investigated cases warrant the submission of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) or Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs), or whether referrals should be closed as non-suspicious with clear, evidence-based justification. 
• Prepare and submit regulatory reports in accordance with applicable legal requirements and jurisdiction-specific reporting timelines. 
• Recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures, including account closures, restrictions, or freezing of funds where necessary and legally applicable. 
• Use blockchain analytics platforms and investigative methodologies to trace transactions, identify suspicious patterns, and assess exposure to illicit financial activities. 
• Provide investigative support to Customer Support, Legal, and other internal teams when handling complex customer cases or requests. 
• Communicate effectively with customers, relevant representatives, and internal legal professionals as required during investigations. 
• Collaborate closely with the Head of the Investigation Team, Chief Compliance Officer, fellow AML Investigators, and other Compliance stakeholders to ensure consistent and effective risk management. 
• Maintain accurate investigation records, document findings, and provide clear reasoning behind decisions and recommendations. 
• Develop and maintain professional relationships with industry peers to exchange knowledge, investigative techniques, and best practices. 
• Continuously strengthen expertise in blockchain technology, virtual currencies, emerging financial crime trends, criminal methodologies, and regulatory developments. 
• Contribute to maintaining robust AML/CTF and sanctions compliance standards across the organization. 

Requirements

• Previous experience in an investigative function, preferably within financial services, cryptocurrency, banking, fintech, or regulatory compliance. 
• Demonstrated experience in Anti-Money Laundering (AML), including Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), AML/CTF investigations, sanctions screening, and SAR/STR reporting. 
• Practical experience using blockchain analytics and investigation tools such as Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic, or equivalent platforms. 
• Basic understanding of blockchain technology, cryptocurrencies, virtual assets, and digital asset transactions, with the willingness to develop deeper technical expertise. 
• Strong knowledge of financial crime risks, including money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud, and sanctions-related activities. 
• University degree or equivalent academic background is preferred. 
• Professional AML certifications, such as Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) or Certified Bitcoin Professional (CBP), are considered an advantage. 
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear investigative reports and communicate findings effectively. 
• Strong critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and decision-making abilities, particularly when assessing complex or ambiguous cases. 
• Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to identify inconsistencies, suspicious patterns, and potential compliance risks. 
• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple investigations while meeting regulatory deadlines. 
• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, exercise sound judgment, and seek guidance when necessary. 
• Flexibility regarding working arrangements and hours, with availability aligned with European time zones. 
• High levels of integrity, accountability, discretion, and professionalism when handling sensitive information.

Key Activities
Oversee group-wide legal and compliance communications
Manage all inbound and outbound communications across the compliance and legal function — ensuring consistency of position, appropriate escalation, and clear audit trails across all CXM Group entities.
Monitor brand, regulatory, and compliance risk
Run ongoing monitoring of online brand exposure and regulatory risk signals across all business verticals and target markets, using dedicated tooling to surface issues before they become regulatory events.
Research target markets and emerging regulatory requirements
Conduct structured research on new and existing jurisdictions — tracking legislative developments, regulatory guidance, and enforcement trends across FX, CFDs, crypto, prediction markets, prop trading, and education to keep the group's risk exposure visible and current.
Build and maintain reporting infrastructure with Ops and IT
Work cross-functionally with Operations and IT to design, implement, and maintain the compliance reporting systems and dashboards needed to give leadership real-time visibility of the group's regulatory posture.
Inventory, organise, and analyse all group legal agreements
Own the end-to-end legal document function: audit existing agreements across all entities, build and maintain the AI-enabled document repository, and ensure all contracts are indexed, cross-referenced, and accessible for rapid retrieval.
Manage regulatory relationships and respond to inquiries
Serve as the primary point of contact for regulators across all jurisdictions — preparing responses, managing ongoing dialogue, and coordinating regulator visits or meetings with appropriate precision and consistency.
Set and enforce contract throughput standards
Define the SLA framework for all internal legal workflows — 24 hours for standard contract reviews, 48 hours for new contract drafting — and hold the Group Paralegal and compliance staff accountable for delivery against those standards. The CCO personally handles high-stakes, novel, or regulator-facing agreements; standard throughput runs through the team.
Key Competences
Two competences are non-negotiable (and typically take a decade of multi-jurisdictional work to build) — everything else can be ramped. If you don't have these, the rest of the profile doesn't matter.
Non-negotiable
Multi-jurisdictional regulatory knowledge
Demonstrated command of tier-one regimes (CySEC, FCA, NFA, ASIC) and offshore/emerging-market frameworks (UAE, Mauritius, Seychelles, SVG, Cambodia), with working knowledge of MiCA and crypto licensing regimes globally. This is the core of the mandate — live deals are already in motion.
Regulator-facing credibility
Confidence and competence in direct regulator engagement — managing inquiries, coordinating responses, and representing the group's compliance posture with consistency across jurisdictions. The group has active regulator relationships that need an owner from day one.
Strong advantage
M&A and licensing fluency
Ability to support acquisition structuring and entity integration from a compliance perspective — assessing regulatory exposure, coordinating with external counsel, and managing parallel licensing processes without dropping threads.
AI-enabled legal operations
Experience deploying AI tooling in legal workflows — document retrieval, contract review acceleration, risk monitoring — is a strong advantage. Candidates without a deployment track record must demonstrate a concrete plan for rapid adoption and the aptitude to execute it.
Function leadership and SLA ownership
Ability to set standards, delegate effectively, and hold a team accountable for throughput — running the contract and compliance function at scale without becoming the bottleneck. Personal involvement reserved for high-stakes, novel, or regulator-facing matters.
Likely Current Job
Chief Compliance Officer (multi-jurisdictional broker or crypto exchange)
The closest equivalent — already holding a CCO title across FX, CFDs, or crypto at a group with multiple regulated entities and active regulator relationships. If your current seat is steady-state and you're ready to own a live build across six asset classes and a dozen jurisdictions, this is the step up.
Head of Compliance (tier-one regulated broker)
One level below CCO at a CySEC, FCA, or ASIC-regulated firm — strong regulatory depth, ready to move into group-level ownership. If you've hit the ceiling of what a single-jurisdiction, single-entity compliance role can teach you, this is where the complexity scales.
Regulatory Affairs Director (fintech or crypto)
Licensing and regulator-facing experience across multiple jurisdictions, possibly without the full compliance function remit yet. If you've been the technical expert behind the licensing programme and want to own the outcome end-to-end, this is the mandate.
M&A Compliance Lead (financial services)
Embedded in acquisition structuring and entity integration at a PE-backed or multi-entity financial services group. If you've been supporting deals from the compliance side and want a seat where M&A fluency is a core expectation rather than a secondary contribution, this is it.
Senior Legal Counsel / Head of Legal (retail broker or crypto exchange)
Contract-heavy, regulator-facing, with compliance responsibility baked in — a common feeder at smaller multi-jurisdictional groups where legal and compliance sit close together. If you've been carrying both functions informally and want a title and mandate that reflects the actual scope, this role makes it official.

Role description

The Risk & Compliance Officer (PCI) is an individual contributor with expert-level domain knowledge, proactive and analytical professional with a strong foundation in risk management principles and control management and monitoring. A demonstrated ability to automate and monitor complex processes is a benefit. They will be responsible for partnering with multiple risk owners and business unit managers to identify the regulatory requirements from an IT perspective for PCI-DSS, SOX, NIS2 and other, and will drive appropriate control monitoring, IT compliance monitoring and implementation. The Risk & Compliance Officer (PCI) partners closely with internal and external PCI audit teams, IT Control owners and Business owners, to ensure consistency, timeliness and especially compliance with the PCI Certification requirements. This person must possess a strong understanding and experience of typical PCI IT And Audit phases and requirements and also exhibit versatility in various PCI tech domains and can build a comprehensive knowledge of the end-to-end Booking IT environment and pertinent PCI controls. 

The Risk & Compliance Officer (PCI) is also a subject matter expert leveraging a deep understanding of the enterprise risk discipline combining deep knowledge of theory and organizational practice or expertise across several different disciplines within a function. Successful risk expertise requires dynamic individuals who are able to liaise with various senior stakeholders and thus need to be articulate communicators, foster collaboration, integrate perspectives and drive to business beneficial outcomes. They will lead the PCI-DSS control efforts to ensure that the PCI requirements are translated into right-sized scalable controls, that audit readiness is maintained throughout the year and that evidence, remediation and risk decisions are coordinated effectively across a complex technology landscape. The role operates as a highly independent first-line risk partner, bridging engineering teams, control owners, internal auditors and external assessors, including QSA. 

This position requires strong stakeholder management skills and requires an individual who can convince others who are skeptical or unwilling to accept new concepts, practices, and approaches.

This role provides a hybrid way of working with an onsite presence of 2 days/week.

Key Job Responsibilities and Duties

• Leads the annual PCI-DSS recertification cycle end-to-end, including planning, scope maintenance, walkthrough preparation, evidence coordination, stakeholder management (follow up, communication, preparation), issue management and support for QSA and audit activities

• Acts as the PCI risk partner to platform, service, payments and engineering teams by translating PCI-DSS requirements into practical control expectations and right-sized guidance for cloud, on-prem and DevOps environments

• Leads PCI scoping reviews and risk assessments for new services, architectural changes and third-party integrations, and determines impacts to the cardholder data environment, connected systems, control design and evidence requirements. 

• Designs, enhances and monitors technical and administrative controls and guardrails that keep PCI compliance embedded in engineering processes rather than added late in the delivery lifecycle. 

• Drives remediation and continuous improvement by tracking deficiencies, performing root cause analysis, coordinating risk-based action plans, standardizing control practices and improving reporting through tools such as JIRA and ServiceNow

• Is responsible for the evidence collection throughout the PCI-DSS recertification process and partnering with the engineering and QSA teams for ensuring timely and complete delivery of the required information. 

Role Qualifications and Requirements

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in Information Security, Technology Risk, IT Audit, Compliance or a related field.

• 5-8 years of relevant experience in IT risk, IT compliance, internal controls, IT audit or security governance, with strong hands-on PCI-DSS experience.

• Demonstrated ownership of PCI-DSS recertification activities, including scope management, evidence collection, walkthrough support, remediation tracking and auditor or QSA engagement.

• Strong knowledge of PCI-DSS requirements, PCI scoping concepts, CDE and connected systems, and artefacts such as AOC, ROC, SAQ and shared-responsibility documentation.

• Experience designing, implementing and monitoring technical and administrative controls in modern technology environments, including cloud, IAM, change management, vulnerability management, logging and monitoring, key management, secure SDLC and segmentation-related controls.

• Experience leading risk assessments, identifying control gaps, performing root cause analysis and driving practical, risk-based remediation.

• Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to challenge constructively, influence engineering teams and translate technical details into clear risk and compliance language for business and audit audiences.

• Strong written and spoken English, with clear and structured communication across cross-functional discussions.

• Familiarity with Jira, ServiceNow and similar reporting or workflow tools used for evidence, issue and compliance tracking.

• Preferred: Professional certifications such as PCI ISA, CISA, CRISC, ISO 27001 or similar.

Benefits & Perks
• Contributing to a high-scale, complex, world renowned product and seeing real-time impact of your work on millions of travelers worldwide

• Working in a fast-paced and performance driven culture

• Technical, behavioral and interpersonal competence advancement via on-the-job opportunities, experimental projects, hackathons, conferences and active community participation

About B2Spin

We are B2Spin, and we are dedicated to delivering the best Free-to-Play Social Casino and gaming experiences by creating captivating, engaging, and unique products that are accessible to everyone. We have built a team of talented professionals from all over the globe, who are working to continually improve the experiences of our players. We are not looking to just be part of the industry, but to revolutionize it.

The role

B2Spin is looking for a Payments & Fraud Data Analyst to join our Business Intelligence team and help keep money moving safely through our platform. You'll turn transactional and player-behaviour data into clear insight that improves payment performance, prevents fraud and abuse, and protects the experience for genuine players — working closely with Payments, Fraud, Compliance and Operations to make their decisions sharper and faster.

What You'll Do

• Own payment performance analytics end to end — diving into success rates, declines, payment methods and provider performance to surface improvements that reduce friction and cost.
• Uncover fraud and abuse patterns across transactional and behavioural data — from promo abuse and multi-accounting to chargebacks and money cycling — and translate findings into actionable rules, thresholds and segments.
• Design, back-test and monitor automated risk decisions, balancing fraud capture against player friction and tracking real-world impact after every change goes live.
• Build the reporting layer that keeps the business informed — dashboards in Looker or Tableau, plus alerts for business-critical anomalies like provider volume drops or risk spikes.
• Partner with Compliance on AML work, delivering investigation queries, data analysis and audit-ready reporting that hold up to scrutiny.
• Accelerate Operations and Customer Service with analytics that quantify review workloads, case outcomes and player-facing friction so teams move faster and more consistently.
• Raise the analytical bar across the business — documenting data sources, metric definitions and automation logic so insight is trusted, reusable and easy to build on.

What We're Looking For

• Hands-on data analyst background in payments, fraud, risk or AML — ideally within gaming, iGaming, fintech or another high-volume digital environment.
• Strong SQL skills on a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred) paired with practical experience in Looker, Tableau or Power BI.
• Demonstrated experience analysing fraud and abuse patterns in transactional and behavioural data, with a clear understanding of the trade-off between fraud capture and friction for genuine players.
• The ability to run analytical projects from ambiguity to delivery — scoping unclear questions, building solutions, documenting them and monitoring their impact over time.
• Confident, clear communication across Operations, Compliance and senior leadership, including the ability to challenge assumptions with data in a remote-team setting.
• An investigative instinct and sharp attention to detail — you notice when something looks off and you follow it until you understand why.
• Python for deeper analysis, anomaly detection or modelling is a strong plus, as is familiarity with fraud-scoring tools, device or behavioural signals, social casino mechanics, or ML approaches to fraud detection.

Our values

At B2Spin, passion means we genuinely love what we build — and we surround ourselves with people who feel the same way. Performance means we back that passion with accountability: we move fast, own our results, and choose progress over perfection every time.

Equal opportunities

We hire based on skills, drive, and ideas — nothing else. Your background, gender, age, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, or educational path will never be a barrier to joining us. We also welcome candidates from non-traditional career journeys and value diverse perspectives that challenge conventional thinking. Diversity fuels our innovation, collaboration, and growth, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can contribute their best work and thrive.

About The GCDO Compliance And Policy Team

The Global Chief Data Office (GCDO) is a global function in PwC recognising the data driven nature of the organisation and enablement of new digital practices. The Compliance and Policy function is responsible for helping PwC’s data assets be proactively and effectively managed, in alignment with global and local regulatory environments, to support the use of data in the global data strategy. The Policy team provides policy expertise to support the governance and responsible use of data in innovation and data handling.

To support these initiatives, we are looking for a data compliance and policy advisor to:

• Support the creation, drafting and approval of both GCDO and network policies. 
• Help develop and implement GCDO strategies, including supporting documentation around client, internal and third party data. 
• Support alignment of the GCDO with the Global Office of Legal Counsel, Global Risk Management and other global functions, developing deep working relationships built on trust. 
• Provide ongoing support of alignment across GCDO pillars with Compliance and Policy functions. 

We are looking for someone with a passion for data and data management, who has strong written and communications skills.

Specific responsibilities of the Data Compliance and Policy Advisor:

• Independently research, collect and analyse information to develop and draft policies to support the Global Data Strategy and all functions across the GCDO. 
• Manage and organise meetings with key global stakeholder groups throughout the document creation process, including information gathering, policy development, and post-publication activities (communicating the published policies to stakeholder groups, completing routine policy refreshes, etc). 
• Manage the development and refresh of multiple policies at one time across multiple stakeholder groups while routinely publishing completed content, using dashboard reporting functionalities. 
• Support territories with data related policy development to facilitate a standardised and cohesive data management approach across the PwC network, consulting with subject matter experts and other PwC departments as necessary. 
• Build relationships with the data leaders, the Chief Data Officer community, and other stakeholder groups to understand their key challenges and working with subject matter experts to address those compliance and policy related challenges. 
• Continue to gain knowledge and develop understanding of data compliance to support all Compliance and Policy Team initiatives. 
• The role reports into the GCDO Compliance Leader and sits within the GCDO Compliance and Policy team. 

Role Requirements:

• 2-3 years experience in professional environment
• Excellent written and oral communication skills
• Experienced policy research, analysis and development skills
• Ability to take a vague and/or ambiguous ask and develop an approach for a path forward
• Business process development and documentation experience
• Strong interest in data management and regulatory compliance
• Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
• Delivering in a highly matrixed, fluid environment
• Collaborating in an international environment, comfortable with flexible working arrangements

About the Team

The compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance culture at the company. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company's AML and regulatory obligations and enterprise risks.

OKX Europe Markets Limited is our MFSA-authorised investment services entity. Its licence covers the operation of a multilateral trading facility alongside our MiFID derivatives business. Operating a trading venue puts a distinct set of obligations on the firm: venue rulebook governance, member admission, market surveillance, transparency and reporting, systems resilience and orderly trading controls. This role owns compliance for that venue.

What You Will Be Doing

As Head of Compliance for the MTF, you will hold the MiFID compliance function for the trading venue and act as the MFSA-approved person for that role. The MLRO function sits separately; you will work alongside the OEM MLRO on financial crime matters that touch venue activity.

You will:

• Own the MTF compliance framework end to end: policies, procedures, controls, registers and the compliance monitoring programme covering MiFID II, MiFIR, MAR and the MFSA Investment Services Rules applicable to MTF operators.

• Act as the primary compliance point of contact for the MFSA on venue matters: authorisation variations, notifications, thematic reviews, RFIs, inspections and remediation.

• Own the venue rulebook. Keep it current, ensure it is enforceable, and run the governance process for changes.

• Oversee member and participant admission: eligibility criteria, non-discriminatory access, direct electronic access arrangements, sponsored access controls, and ongoing monitoring of members' compliance with the rules of the venue.

• Oversee admission to trading of financial instruments, including the compliance assessment of new instruments, product classes and tokenised or DLT-based instruments where relevant.

• Provide compliance oversight of orderly trading requirements: systems capacity and resilience, testing of members' algorithms, circuit breakers, order-to-trade ratios, tick sizes, market making schemes and clock synchronisation.

• Provide compliance oversight of pre- and post-trade transparency, waivers and deferrals, transaction reporting, reference data and the accuracy and completeness controls behind them.

• Advise the business on the interaction between the MTF and OKX's wider European footprint: the MiFID derivatives business, MiCA-authorised activity in OKX Europe Ltd, and the DLT Pilot Regime where a DLT MTF is in scope.

• Build, lead and develop the MTF compliance team, and set the compliance training curriculum for venue-facing staff, trading operations and technology.

• Experience preparing and defending compliance reporting to a board or regulator.

8ef49032d696.description:
Are you ready to join our digital revolution journey?

At Aleph , we’re not just part of the digital advertising landscape—we’re shaping its future. Representing the world’s leading platforms, including TikTok, Amazon, Google, and nearly 55 others, we operate in 130+ markets across new and existing geographies.

Our mission is to empower advertisers and brands to unlock the full potential of these platforms' advertising capabilities. By fostering long-lasting partnerships, we create limitless opportunities for people and businesses to advertise effectively at both local and global levels.

With a presence spanning continents, Aleph offers you the chance to be part of a fast-growing, innovative team where your work makes a direct impact. If you’re ambitious, forward-thinking, and eager to thrive in a dynamic, global environment, Aleph is the perfect place to build your career.

At Aleph, we're committed to ensuring that all of our customers' and partners' data is protected and that our work complies with data protection legislation across the markets we operate in — including as AI regulation reshapes that landscape. We're looking for an experienced AI Tech and Data Privacy Associate Manager (or Manager, depending on experience), to join our global team and help manage sensitive information, support contract preparation, carry out data protection assessments, and advise on the growing intersection of AI governance and privacy compliance across our global footprint.

What You Will Do

• Advise on and support the practical implementation of legal requirements across all AI risk categories (e.g., under the EU AI Act — prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk, and minimal-risk systems), including risk classification, compliance obligations, and coordination with product and tech teams.
• Monitor emerging AI regulations more broadly and advise on their intersection with data protection across our markets.
• Advise the business on responsible AI governance and internal AI use policies.
• Advise, coordinate, and support colleagues across the business on data protection and privacy compliance issues, including in non-EU markets.
• Collaborate on internal audits at Aleph Group level in the field of data protection.
• Help prepare reports, presentations, and educational materials on data protection, privacy, and AI compliance topics.
• Participate in data protection, privacy, and AI-related legal projects.
• Promote a strong culture of data protection and responsible AI compliance across Aleph.
• Support AI-related technology projects, including API integrations with third-party AI providers, ensuring data protection, IP, and contractual compliance throughout implementation.
• Negotiate and draft agreements related to AI/technology procurement (vendor contracts, API and data-sharing agreements, licensing terms), including IP protection, ownership, and indemnification provisions.
• Coordinate with product, tech, and other teams to assess IP, confidentiality, and data protection risks before onboarding new AI tools or vendors.
• Organize and maintain data protection records and related documentation at a global level.
• Support the preparation of contracts with business partners and other legal documents (for example, internal policies) in the field of data protection and GDPR compliance.
• Carry out Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) together with the wider team.
• Take on other ad hoc legal and compliance-related tasks as needed.

What We Are Looking For

• A degree in Law.
• Minimum 4–6 years of hands-on experience in data privacy and compliance, with a strong focus on GDPR — this is not an entry-level role.
• Solid expertise in data privacy laws and practices, including a deep understanding of GDPR.
• Hands-on experience completing legal/compliance requirements for the implementation of AI systems across all risk categories (e.g., under the EU AI Act), including but not limited to high-risk systems — this is a requirement, not just a plus.
• Working knowledge of AI-related legal and regulatory frameworks more broadly.
• Demonstrated ability to research and apply data privacy requirements in non-EU markets (LATAM, APAC, and/or MEA), given our global operating footprint.
• Proficient English communication skills, written and verbal — this is a must.
• A tech-oriented mindset, genuine curiosity about how AI and emerging technologies intersect with privacy law, and strong motivation to continuously learn new legal frameworks and compliance tools.
• Experience working in a global or regional setting, with the ability to operate confidently outside a single-market (EU-only) focus.
• Practical experience negotiating and drafting technology/AI related agreements (vendor contracts, API and data-sharing agreements, licensing terms), including IP protection, ownership, and indemnification provisions.

Why Join Aleph

• Shape data protection and AI governance practice at scale: your work will directly protect the trust of Aleph's customers and partners across a global footprint spanning Europe, LATAM, APAC and MEA.
• Apply AI compliance expertise at scale: you'll drive real implementation work across the full spectrum of AI risk categories as regulation matures, not just policy-watching.
• Build deep expertise fast: exposure to DPIAs, cross-border data transfers, AI risk assessments, and multi-jurisdictional privacy frameworks gives you a faster path to becoming a recognized privacy expert than most single-market roles.
• Join a growing, collaborative legal team based in Warsaw that values mentorship and hands-on learning over hierarchy.

In line with the EU Pay Transparency Directive, we are committed to fair and open compensation practices. The minimum gross annual base salary is RON 184,000, with the final level (Associate Manager or Manager) and offer reflecting your experience, skills, and scope of the role.

In addition to base salary, this role includes a variable component, paid annually.

Why Join Us?

Aleph is a place of many cultures, perspectives, and talents. We support each other, creating an environment of giving and receiving. We value partnership and communication because we believe it takes a group of people to achieve great things. We are energized by our ever-changing industry, our curiosity keeps us learning and seeking out new opportunities.

We stay flexible and adaptable, and believe in moving with the speed of change. We encourage everyone to strive for more, providing our internal talent with growth opportunities and the ability to learn together.

#ALEPH

We use Lever, our recruitment management platform, which includes AI-powered features that may assist our hiring team in reviewing applications, analyzing CVs, and identifying relevant qualifications. These tools support - but do not replace - human judgement. All hiring decisions are made by people. For more information about how your personal data is processed, including your rights in relation to AI-assisted processing, please see our Candidate Privacy Policy or contact us at [email protected] .

IT Risk & Compliance Security Specialist (Cybersecurity & IT Infrastructure Team)

The Risk and Compliance Security Specialist will play an important role in implementing and managing the risk and compliance programs related to IT security. This position involves assessing, identifying, and mitigating risks, as well as ensuring the company's IT infrastructure complies with requisite standards and regulations.

What you’ll have to do:

Governance:

• Develop, implement, and maintain a robust IT security program aligned with regulatory and industry standards (ISO 27001, DORA, NIS2, PCI DSS, NIST CSF).
• Collaborate with senior leadership and business stakeholders to foster awareness of risk and compliance across the organization.
• Promote best practices and ensure alignment with broader governance objectives.
• Establish security baselines for both on-premises and cloud-based environments.
• Create and maintain IT governance policies, including access control, change management, data retention, and business continuity.
• Develop and maintain an incident response plan, ensuring a structured approach for detecting, containing, and recovering from security breaches.
• Conduct regular training sessions for employees to raise awareness of IT risk and compliance issues.

Risk Management:

• Implement a robust IT risk management framework that supports proactive identification, assessment, mitigation, and monitoring of risks.
• Regularly review and update the framework to reflect changes in the internal and external environment.
• Conduct periodic IT risk assessments to identify vulnerabilities, assess potential impacts, and develop mitigation strategies.
• Collaborate with IT and business units to develop risk mitigation plans and ensure timely implementation.
• Run the third-party risk management process, including security due diligence for new suppliers, contractual security requirements, and periodic reassessment of critical vendors, in line with NIS2 supply chain security requirements.
• Manage a risk register, ensuring that identified risks are continuously monitored and addressed.
• Manage the risk acceptance and policy exception process, ensuring exceptions are documented, approved by the appropriate risk owners, time-bound, and periodically reviewed.

Compliance:

• Monitor regulatory changes and ensure organizational compliance with relevant laws and regulations (e.g., GDPR, DORA, NIS2, PCI DSS).
• Track regulatory requirements across the countries where we operate (Romania, Hungary, Bulgaria), including national NIS2 transpositions, and assess their impact on the organization.
• Coordinate mandatory incident notifications to competent authorities and national CSIRTs (e.g., DNSC in Romania), ensuring reports are submitted within NIS2 timelines.
• Coordinate internal and external IT audits, ensuring all compliance requirements are met.
• Act as the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) for auditors, managing collaboration throughout audit engagements, from information requests and evidence collection to follow-up on findings and remediation actions.
• Ensure documentation is accurate, up-to-date, and readily accessible for audits and governance reviews.
• Plan and perform periodic testing of security controls to verify their design and operating effectiveness, and track remediation of identified gaps.

Performance Measurement and Reporting:

• Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics to measure the effectiveness of IT risk and compliance programs.
• Provide regular reports and updates to governance bodies on progress, challenges, and areas for improvement.
• Contribute to periodic technology risk reporting to the group and shareholders, ensuring the accuracy and consistency of risk and compliance data.

What makes you a good fit:

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Relevant certifications such as CISA, CRISC, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer / Lead Auditor, or equivalent are preferred.
• Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in IT risk management or IT compliance.
• Extensive knowledge of industry standards and frameworks like ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT, etc.
• Practical experience with regulatory compliance requirements such as NIS2, DORA, PCI DSS, and GDPR.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Proficiency in using IT risk management tools and software.
• Experience with cloud security and compliance considerations.
• Strong understanding of IT security principles and best practices.
• Ability to interpret and apply regulatory requirements to IT environments.
• Familiarity with emerging IT risks and trends, such as cyber threats, data privacy, and digital transformation.
• Strong organizational and multitasking skills.
• Experience with auditing and monitoring tools.

The Compliance function is responsible for promoting a strong compliance culture and supporting the safe, sustainable growth of OKX. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on regulatory obligations, conduct expectations and enterprise risks.

OKX Europe Limited operates within a significant EU regulatory perimeter, including authorisation as a crypto-asset service provider under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation and as a payment institution in Malta.

As Deputy Head of Compliance for OKX Europe Limited, you will support the Head of Compliance in leading the entity’s Compliance function and maintaining an effective compliance framework across its crypto-asset and payment services.

You will oversee the day-to-day operation of key elements of the compliance programme, provide trusted advice to senior stakeholders and deputise for the Head of Compliance when required. You will help translate regulatory requirements into practical controls and ensure that compliance considerations are embedded in products, services and strategic decisions.

The position reports to the Head of Compliance, OKX Europe Limited, with appropriate access to local senior management, Board committees and relevant regional and global Compliance leaders.

• Reporting: Prepare high-quality reports on key risks, trends, breaches, and monitoring findings for senior management, Boards, and committees.

• Knowledge of EU regulatory requirements relating to safeguarding, stablecoins, outsourcing, operational resilience, consumer protection and cross-border passporting.

As a Product Owner you will be accountable for maximizing the value of changes delivered to customers, users and internal stakeholders with your multidisciplinary agile team. The changes delivered may be purely IT technical, non-technical and more commonly a combination. You will be the primary interface to internal and external customers / users, managing stakeholder expectations and engaging them throughout e.g. the sponsor, scaled agile team members (where applicable), related agile and non-agile teams, control functions and other stakeholders.

As a Product Owner you will also be accountable for synthesizing stakeholder needs and shaping the overall agile team mission, product vision, scope, desired business outcomes and delivery roadmap with your team. As a “servant-leader”, you will enable the agile team to work effectively by articulating the stakeholder situation, the desired outcomes and why the specific scope is being prioritised. As part of your interface role, you will collaborate with stakeholders including their agile team members to negotiate requirements, shape the product vision, define the delivery roadmap, keep stakeholders informed of status, obtain feedback on agile team outputs, agree implementation steps and ensure value is being realised.

As a Product Owner you will also be accountable for creating, prioritizing and maintaining the product backlog with your agile team, that contains details of all short and medium-term agile team deliverables, each of which with a defined scope, measurable outcomes and acceptance criteria. For each iteration/sprint, you will be responsible for selecting user stories you wish to prioritise for delivery, you discuss the proposed iteration/sprint scope with the agile team, address any clarifying questions and agree on the iteration/sprint scope. You will be a constant source of guidance and review feedback; you will accept completed work products which meet the defined acceptance criteria.

In partnership with the Scrum Master/Agile Coach, you will create an environment of psychological safety which brings out the best in each agile team member, while encouraging the agile team to self-direct their work, to innovate and effectively apply their skills & creativity to deliver the product backlog.
