Why Verifone

For more than 40 years Verifone has established a remarkable record of leadership in the electronic payment technology industry. Verifone has one of the leading electronic payment solutions brands and is one of the largest providers of electronic payment systems worldwide.

Verifone has a diverse, dynamic and fast paced work environment in which employees are focused on results and have opportunities to excel. We take pride in the fact that we work with leading retailers, merchants, banks, and third party partners to invent and deliver innovative payments solution around the world. We strive for excellence in our products and services, and are obsessed with customer happiness. Across the globe, Verifone employees are leading the payments industry through experience, innovation, and an ambitious spirit. Whether it’s developing the next platform of secure payment systems or searching for new ways to bring electronic payments to new markets, the team at Verifone is dedicated to the success of our customers, partners and investors. It is this passion for innovation that drives each one of our employees for personal and professional success.

Verifone is proudly an in-office work culture as we see immense benefits to career development and business results from our colleagues being physically co-located.

What's Exciting About The Role

As Merchant Monitoring & Ongoing Due Diligence (ODD) Analyst, you keep our existing merchant portfolio compliant with the applicable AML/CTF frameworks (GwG, Wwft, MLR 2017, FIN-FSA AML Act, EBA guidelines) and internal group risk appetite. You review, refresh and re-assess merchant files on a risk-based cycle, act on trigger events from monitoring signals, and make well-documented decisions on continuation, remediation or exit – all under a single group standard applied across entities.

Merchant Monitoring & ODD is being built out as a dedicated capability within the group. This role is deliberately designed with a growth path: strong performers will have the opportunity to grow into the Team Lead Merchant Monitoring & ODD position as the function scales.

Key Responsibilities

• Periodic reviews: Execute risk-based re-underwriting cycles (low / medium / high / EDD) across the group merchant portfolio, applying the entity-specific policy that governs each merchant (BaFin / DNB / FCA / FIN-FSA) on top of the common group standard.
• Trigger-based reviews: Handle event-driven reviews originating from transaction monitoring (Featurespace / IBM Safer Payments), adverse media, sanctions or PEP hits, UBO or legal-form changes, chargeback spikes and scheme notifications.
• KYC / KYB refresh: Re-verify legal entity data, UBO structures, control persons, licensing, PoA and business model; refresh IDs, register extracts and financials; document sources and gaps.
• Screening & investigations: Clear sanctions, PEP and adverse media alerts; conduct open-source and register-based investigations; escalate confirmed matches to the MLRO / 2nd Line.
• Enhanced due diligence: Build EDD files for high-risk merchants (high-risk industries, complex ownership, offshore nexus, cash-intensive business), including SoW/SoF where relevant.
• Risk decisions: Recommend continuation, remediation actions, restrictions or off-boarding; draft clear rationales that hold up in internal audit, external audit (Grant Thornton, fscom, Forvis Mazars) and supervisory review by any of the group’s regulators (BaFin, DNB, FCA, FIN-FSA).
• Quality & controls: Follow the 4-eyes principle, maintain complete audit trails in the KYC case management tool (Sumsub and internal systems) and contribute to sample selection for internal QA.
• Cross-functional work: Interface with Onboarding, Credit Risk, Fraud, AML/Compliance (2nd Line MLROs across entities), Sales and Merchant Support; support group regulatory projects (DORA/ZAIT remediation, DNB and BaFin submissions, FCA / FIN-FSA responses) where re-underwriting evidence is required. 

Skills And Experience We Desire

• Experience: 3–7 years of hands-on KYC/KYB experience in a payment institution, acquirer, PSP, e-money institution or bank; demonstrable ownership of periodic reviews and EDD, not only onboarding.
• Regulatory knowledge: Solid working knowledge of at least one European AML/CTF framework (GwG, Wwft, MLR 2017, FIN-FSA AML Act or equivalent) and card scheme rules (Visa, Mastercard); readiness to apply the group standard across entities. Familiarity with EBA ML/TF risk factor guidelines expected; BaFin AuA, DNB Wwft guidance or FCA FCG are all valued.
• Risk mindset: Able to form and defend a risk view on complex merchant structures – holding companies, nominee arrangements, marketplaces, PayFac and high-risk MCCs.
• Tools: Comfortable with KYC platforms (e.g. Sumsub, LexisNexis, Dow Jones, World-Check), transaction monitoring systems and standard investigative sources (Handelsregister, Companies House, KVK, OpenCorporates).

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken's Market Surveillance function is responsible for detecting, investigating and reporting market abuse across our regulated trading venues, spanning spot crypto markets, crypto futures, tokenised equities, OTC markets and consumer trading. As our licensing footprint and product range grow, so does the scale and complexity of the surveillance programme behind them.

We are hiring several Senior Compliance Associates to carry out day to day surveillance across our markets, investigate what that surveillance uncovers, and help us build the programme out as the business grows.

The opportunity

• Review and disposition surveillance alerts across our regulated markets, and record the reasoning behind each decision clearly enough that someone else can follow it.
• Carry out analytical reviews that begin with trade and order data rather than with a system-generated alert.
• Investigate escalated behaviour end to end: gather the data, reconstruct what happened, and write it up for presentation to senior compliance stakeholders.
• Assess referrals raised from across the business and externally, and take forward the ones that warrant it.
• Draft suspicious transaction and order reports and suspicious activity reports.
• Produce management information and regulatory reporting for the entities we cover.
• Contribute to surveillance platform and tooling work, including bringing new products and data sources into scope and testing that detection behaves as intended.
• Use AI and automation tools to speed up evidence-gathering and case reconstruction, with human judgement over the final call. 

What You Bring

• At least 2 years experience in trade surveillance, market abuse investigation or trading conduct inside a regulated firm, such as an exchange, broker-dealer, trading venue, bank or comparable regulated trading business.
• Working knowledge of the core market abuse typologies, for example spoofing, layering, wash trading, insider dealing, front running and ramping.
• Experience reviewing and dispositioning surveillance alerts, and writing up what you found to a standard others can rely on.
• Clear, evidence-first written communication. Your case files and escalations will sometimes be read by auditors and regulators without you in the room to explain them.
• Comfort using generative AI and other automation tools to improve the speed and quality of investigative work, while maintaining the oversight that regulated casework requires.
• Based in the UK, Ireland, Cyprus, Malta, Romania or Canada, with fluency in English. 

Nice to haves

• Exposure to crypto-asset markets is welcomed but not required.
• Hands-on use of a surveillance platform such as Scila, Nasdaq SMARTS, Eventus or NICE Actimize.
• SQL or a similar query tool for evidence-gathering.
• Experience drafting suspicious transaction and order reports or suspicious activity reports.
• Electronic communications surveillance experience.

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City, CertiK provides end-to-end security solutions including smart contract audits, penetration testing, on-chain monitoring, incident response, and compliance services for some of the largest projects in the digital asset ecosystem.

Today, CertiK supports thousands of enterprise clients and Web3 projects globally, with a distributed international team spanning North America, Asia, and Europe. The company is backed by leading investors including Coatue, Goldman Sachs, Insight Partners, and Sequoia Capital, and has been recognized by organizations such as the World Economic Forum and CB Insights for its contributions to blockchain security innovation.

About You 
You are proactive, reliable, and enjoy helping people solve problems. You are highly organized, eager to learn, and comfortable supporting both technical and non-technical teams. You enjoy being hands-on, can adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment, and are willing to take ownership of day-to-day operational tasks to help keep the office and systems running smoothly.

About the Role 
We are looking for a Web3 Licensing and Regulatory Compliance Specialist to support client delivery and develop our Web3 regulatory services. You will work with our InfoSec and Compliance Lead and CertiK specialists across cybersecurity, AML, product, and engineering to turn regulatory requirements into practical plans, application materials, and controls. The role combines client assignments with regulatory research and internal development for crypto-asset service providers, virtual asset service providers, token issuers, and other digital-asset businesses in the European Union, the United Arab Emirates, and other priority jurisdictions.

Responsibilities

Client Delivery

• 
Deliver Web3 regulatory advisory projects, including licensing and authorisation readiness, gap assessments, compliance reviews, and implementation support for CASPs, VASPs, token issuers, and other digital-asset businesses.

• 
Help clients translate regulatory requirements into practical governance, AML and CFT, cybersecurity, technology, and operational controls, drawing on CertiK's wider expertise.

• 
Support application-related work by coordinating key materials, evidence, stakeholders, and responses to regulators, particularly for European Union and United Arab Emirates processes.

• 
Present clear findings and recommendations in reports and workshops, and manage delivery across agreed scope, timelines, and follow-up actions.

Regulatory Research and Internal Product and Service Development

• 
Monitor and analyse Web3 regulation and supervisory expectations across priority jurisdictions, with particular attention to the European Union and the United Arab Emirates.

• 
Turn regulatory research and client experience into reusable methods, templates, control mappings, knowledge materials, and new or updated regulatory service offerings.

• 
Work with CertiK's cybersecurity, AML, product, and engineering teams to develop and improve compliance tools and workflows, including requirements definition, regulatory content, and testing.

Use market developments and client feedback to identify opportunities to improve our tools and services and make delivery more consistent and scalable.

Requirements

Strong match: Hands-on experience supporting a Web3 licensing or authorisation process for a CASP, VASP, token issuer, or similar digital-asset business. Direct application experience under MiCA, VARA, ADGM FSRA, DFSA, or another European Union or United Arab Emirates regime is especially valuable.

• 
Experience: Two to four years in digital-asset regulatory compliance, financial-services licensing, legal or compliance operations, consulting, or a related role.

Web3 knowledge: Practical understanding of blockchain networks, wallets, custody, exchanges, transfers, token issuance, stablecoins, and common digital-asset business models.

Regulatory knowledge: Working knowledge of governance, operational risk, consumer protection, technology, cybersecurity, and/or AML requirements relevant to digital-asset firms.

What We Offer

• 
Competitive compensation: A competitive base salary plus equity or token options where applicable.

• 
Professional growth: Direct exposure to EU, UAE, and global digital-asset authorisation projects, with support to deepen your Web3 regulatory expertise.

This role must be performed outside the United States. We are unable to consider candidates who will work from within the U.S.

Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub.

This position is for a Cyber Security Compliance Manager in the Solutions Services Group (SSG). This is an exciting role that will give you the opportunity to work with Lenovo Product teams around the world to help Lenovo Business Units align with various regional, national and international security standards and regulations. You will be working alongside some of the best security teams in the industry. You will join a growing team of security professionals to help assess risk, ensure compliance and to design risk remediation and mitigation strategies and tactics. 

This role will work hand in hand with business executives, product managers, architects, engineers, devops, and developers to support operationalization of cybersecurity compliance program to meet regulatory obligations with a primary focus on the EU Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2) and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA).

What You Will Do

• Lead NIS2 CRA compliance readiness by conducting gap assessments, identifying risks, and translating findings into clear, prioritized remediation plans.
• Partner with engineering and product teams to embed Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) requirements into the product lifecycle, including secure-by-design principles, vulnerability management, SBOMs, and incident reporting processes.
• Drive implementation of cybersecurity and risk management controls, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements related to governance, accountability, supply chain security, and operational resilience.
• Manage compliance programs and projects end-to-end, defining timelines, milestones, and deliverables while proactively tracking progress, risks, dependencies, and blockers.
• Act as the primary liaison across SSG, collaborating with security, legal, engineering, product, procurement, and leadership teams on NIS2 and CRA compliance initiatives.
• Develop and maintain compliance frameworks and documentation, including policies, procedures, control matrices, evidence repositories, audit trails, and supporting records.
• Support internal and external audits, assessments, and regulatory engagements, ensuring the organization is prepared for compliance reviews and regulator inquiries.
• Monitor evolving cybersecurity regulations and industry standards, including ENISA guidance and harmonized standards, while delivering metrics, reporting, and insights that measure program maturity and communicate compliance status to leadership.

What You Will Need

• 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity compliance, governance, risk compliance (GRC), IT/cyber risk management, or a related regulatory compliance function.
• Strong knowledge of EU cybersecurity regulations, including NIS2 and the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), or experience with frameworks such as GDPR, DORA, and ISO 27001 with the ability to quickly build expertise in emerging regulations.
• Proven experience developing, implementing, or maturing compliance programs, helping organizations strengthen governance, controls, and regulatory readiness.
• Excellent project management skills, with the ability to independently lead multiple initiatives, manage competing priorities, and coordinate complex cross-functional workstreams.
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing capabilities, comfortable partnering with engineering, product, legal, procurement, security, and executive leadership teams to drive alignment and execution.
• Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, cybersecurity, and regulatory requirements into clear, practical guidance for both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Law, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and practical experience.
• Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or similar are preferred, along with cybersecurity experience within a technology company, managed services provider (MSP), or connected-product organization operating under Cyber Resilience Act requirements.

What We Offer

• An international team with a high focus on Gender Diversity.
• Employee Assistance Program, e.g., for psychological, legal financial consultancy. 
• You are joining a company that prioritizes sustainable solutions like CO2 Offset, Asset Recovery Services, and the Lenovo Certified Refurbished portfolio.

Companie: Urbio - Leading Smart Street Lighting Manufacturing Company in Eastern Europe
Locație: Birou, Iași - normă întreagă, contract pe perioadă nedeterminată; deplasări doar cu titlu excepțional
Departament: BID (Bid & Compliance)
Subordonare directă: Compliance Team Leader

Despre Urbio
Urbio este un producător european de top de soluții inteligente pentru iluminatul stradal, cu peste 3.000 de proiecte livrate cu succes în România, Republica Moldova, Serbia și Muntenegru.
Suntem specializați în corpuri de iluminat inteligente, eficiente energetic și înalt certificate, integrate nativ cu ecosistemul nostru de soluții, care include:
· O platformă smart city bazată pe AI pentru managementul activelor și al iluminatului;
· Controlere, senzori și accesorii smart avansate;
· O gamă largă de protocoale de comunicație, inclusiv PLC, LoRa și GSM.
Fiecare proiect pe care îl câștigăm începe cu o ofertă corectă și conformă. Căutăm un inginer riguros care să se asigure că partea tehnică a ofertelor noastre răspunde complet și verificabil cerințelor fiecărei proceduri.
Prezentarea rolului
Compliance Engineer asigură conformitatea tehnică a ofertelor depuse de grup la proceduri de achiziție publică și privată. Demonstrează, documentat și verificabil, că produsele și soluțiile propuse îndeplinesc cerințele caietului de sarcini, ale normativelor și ale standardelor aplicabile.
Responsabilități principale
Analiză și conformitate tehnică
· Analizează documentațiile de atribuire (caiet de sarcini, fișa de date, clarificări) și extrage cerințele tehnice minime și factorii de evaluare tehnici.
· Verifică conformitatea produselor și echipamentelor propuse cu cerințele procedurii și semnalează din timp neconformitățile și riscurile de respingere.
· Propune soluții tehnice echivalente sau alternative, justificate tehnic, atunci când produsul standard nu acoperă cerința.
· Utilizează instrumentele digitale ale companiei pentru îndeplinirea sarcinilor de serviciu.
Întocmirea părții tehnice a ofertei
· Întocmește fișe tehnice de conformitate (cerință vs. ofertat, cu trimitere la documentul justificativ).
· Realizează simulări luminotehnice în DIALux evo pentru iluminat public și arhitectural, conform SR EN 13201 și normelor aplicabile.
· Elaborează breviare de calcul (dimensionări electrice, căderi de tensiune, calcul de consum și economie de energie, dimensionări fotovoltaice și de stocare, după caz).
· Colectează și verifică documentele suport: fișe tehnice ale producătorului, certificate, declarații de conformitate CE, rapoarte de încercări (LM-79, LM-80, IP, IK etc.).
· Contribuie la propunerea tehnică împreună cu Bid Specialist și la răspunsurile la solicitările de clarificări ale autorităților contractante.
Organizare și calitate
· Respectă calendarul procedurilor și termenele stabilite.
· Lucrează pe sarcinile atribuite în instrumentele digitale ale companiei și actualizează statusul acestora.
· Întreține biblioteca internă de fișe tehnice, fotometrii (fișiere LDT/IES), simulări și breviare tip.
· Urmărește modificările legislative și normative din domeniu (standarde de iluminat, normative electrice, cerințe de eficiență energetică).
· Asigură back-up pentru colegii din echipa de compliance la vârfuri de activitate.
· Îndeplinește alte sarcini în aria de competență, stabilite de Compliance Team Leader.

Cerințe obligatorii
· Studii superioare inginerești finalizate cu diplomă de licență: ingineria instalațiilor, inginerie energetică, inginerie electrică, electrotehnică, electronică și telecomunicații sau domenii similare.
· Cunoștințe de lucru în DIALux (de preferat DIALux evo): modelare, import fotometrii, rapoarte de calcul.
· Capacitatea de a citi și interpreta caiete de sarcini, scheme electrice și fișe tehnice de produs.
· Utilizare avansată MS Office (Word, Excel), Adobe Acrobat pentru lucrul cu documente PDF.
· Limba engleză – nivel minim B2, scris și citit, nivel tehnic.
Constituie avantaj
· Atestat ANRE de electrician autorizat, minim gradul IIA.
· Experiență de minim 1–2 ani în ofertare tehnică, proiectare sau execuție de instalații electrice / iluminat public.
· Permis de conducere categoria B.
· Cunoașterea legislației achizițiilor publice (Legea 98/2016, HG 395/2016) și a platformei SEAP/SICAP.
· Cunoașterea standardelor SR EN 13201 (iluminat rutier) și SR EN 12464 (iluminat interior/exterior la locurile de muncă).
· Cunoștințe AutoCAD și ale altor programe de calcul (Relux, programe de dimensionare electrică sau fotovoltaică, ex. PVsyst).
· Experiență cu sisteme de telegestiune pentru iluminat public, surse fotovoltaice sau stocare de energie.
· O a doua limbă străină.

Candidatul ideal
· Riguros și atent la detalii: o singură neconformitate poate duce la respingerea ofertei.
· Capabil să lucreze sub presiunea termenelor și să gestioneze mai multe proceduri în paralel.
· Cu gândire analitică și capacitate de sinteză a documentațiilor tehnice voluminoase.
· Comunică clar, în scris și verbal, cu colegii din BID, producție și vânzări.
· Are spirit de echipă, este proactiv și dispus să învețe (instrumente digitale și AI folosite în departament).
· Dă dovadă de integritate și confidențialitate față de informațiile comerciale și tehnice ale ofertelor.
Sprijinul de care vei beneficia
Vei lucra îndeaproape cu Bid Specialist, Financial Bid Specialist și Supply Chain Compliance Engineer, precum și cu echipele de Vânzări, Producție și Achiziții/Logistică. Vei avea la dispoziție laptop, licență software de proiectare, acces la instrumentele digitale ale departamentului și un program de formare: produsele grupului, metodologia de ofertare, cursuri de specializare și sprijin pentru obținerea sau ridicarea gradului atestatului ANRE.
Ce oferim
· Activitate preponderent de birou; deplasările (vizite în teren, întâlniri cu beneficiari sau parteneri) sunt cu titlu excepțional și se decontează integral.
· Program de lucru: luni–vineri, 8 ore/zi; la vârfuri de termene poate fi necesară flexibilitate.
· Salariu motivant, corelat cu experiența, și bonusuri legate de rezultatele departamentului [de completat].
· Expunere la proiecte naționale și internaționale și drum de evoluție către roluri de coordonare.
· Beneficii suplimentare: tichete de masă și asigurare medicală privată.

Te vei alătura unei echipe de colegi implicați și capabili, care sunt mândri de ceea ce construim - oameni cărora le pasă ca detaliile să fie corecte și care caută mereu să ne îmbunătățim procesele, astfel încât fiecare ofertă să plece la timp și complet conformă.

Dacă vrei să fii persoana care se asigură că fiecare ofertă tehnică este impecabilă, ne-ar face plăcere să te cunoaștem!

You will work within the vertical Group Data Protection Compliance, a department within Compliance that is in place starting March 2023. Data Protection Compliance is an important risk area with growing interest from both internal and external stakeholders.

As a Global Data Protection Compliance Specialist, you are (or can become) an expert on the area of Data Protection Risk Management, as this is a key compliance risk that the bank needs to manage. Other topics can be related to challenge and advise activities on bank wide risks, such as storage limitation, third party data processors and cookie compliance but also formulating 2nd line responses on new and emerging risks.

What You’ll Bring To The Team

• You have excellent collaboration skills and ability to work across functional and geographic lines;

dc5fb64830dd.description:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken's Compliance Operations teams, including the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), investigations and enhanced due diligence, are the front line of how Kraken detects and responds to financial crime. The systems they run on sit within Core Services Product, alongside the engineering teams who build them. That covers alert ingestion, case management, investigator tooling and a growing set of automation and AI tools.

This role owns the product for that investigation platform. That means how an alert is created, enriched, grouped and suppressed. How it becomes a case. How an investigator reaches and documents a decision. And how every step is evidenced to a regulator or auditor. You'll start with the FIU, where the workflows are most complex and the audit bar is highest, then extend the platform across Compliance Operations.

The opportunity

• Own the investigation-platform roadmap end to end. Sequence it and defend it, and re-sequence it when a regulator or the RCO raises a P0.
• Define "done" before build starts. Write phased deliverables and acceptance criteria that Compliance signs off, and hold the line when scope moves.
• Get requirements in before engineering starts. Build the intake between Compliance policy, monitoring rules and case management so that changes don't reach investigators before their workflows are ready.
• Understand the process before building. Reconcile policy and SOPs against what investigators actually do and what the system actually does. Know the difference between a process fix and a technical one, and say which requests are in scope for engineering.
• Understand the pipeline well enough to challenge it: ingestion, profile and transaction resolution, suppression and grouping logic, and reconciliation between vendor output and case management. Be able to walk an auditor through it with live examples.
• Make auditability a first-class requirement: audit trail, data lineage, evidence retention, reviewer attribution, change-management controls, and validation of filtering and suppression logic.
• Ship automation and AI into regulated workflows with controls that hold up in Compliance, IT and privacy audits. That means human-in-the-loop design, explainability and ongoing monitoring.
• Run the operating rhythm: a shared forum with engineering and adjacent product managers, a regular stakeholder update, and one delivery status that everyone reads the same way.

What You Bring

• 4+ years of product management, including 2+ years on financial-crime systems such as transaction monitoring, investigations, case management, KYC/EDD or sanctions screening.
• Working knowledge of how an AML programme is examined, including the questions regulators, internal audit and model validation ask about monitoring, filing and control systems.
• The technical fluency to go deep on data flows and system design with engineers, and to spot when a design won't meet the requirement.
• A track record of shipping internal tools or operational platforms that measurably changed how an operations team works.
• Clear, concise writing, from PRDs and phase plans to audit walkthroughs and executive updates.
• The judgement to tell a senior stakeholder a timeline isn't realistic because the requirements aren't written yet, and to keep the relationship intact.

Nice to haves

• Direct FIU experience, such as alert disposition, SAR/STR filing or leading investigators.
• Crypto or digital-asset experience, such as blockchain analytics, wallet-level transaction analysis or focal vs counterparty logic.
• Experience shipping AI or ML into a regulated investigative workflow, including the control design.
• Build-vs-buy and vendor evaluation for monitoring or case-management tooling.
• Experience with programmes that span jurisdictions (UK, EU/MiCA, US).

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Our commitment
